$comment: False positives and deliberate non-translatables for scripts/i18n-inventory.mjs. Every entry needs a reason; tests/i18n-inventory.node.test.ts rejects a missing reason and an entry that matches nothing. Match is substring on the finding text, exact on file and (when present) category.

exceptions.reason: SEW gearmotor type designation from the bundled AASX digital nameplate — a device model number that must match the asset, so translating it would break the link to the datasheet.
Product name in the version footer. Translating a brand would make the build string unsearchable in support threads and release notes; the surrounding tooltip IS translated (settings:version.title).

Deliberately bilingual, for the same reason the locale list uses endonyms (LanguageSection.tsx): whoever needs this control cannot read the language the UI is currently in. Routing it through the catalog would render it in one language only — and would put CJK in en-US, which tests/i18n-catalog.node.test.ts rejects.
Sample signal path shown as a preview of each chip variant. PS-I18N-001 §2 / ADR-0001 §6 keep signal names untranslated, so a translated example would show a form no PLC ever emits.

Placeholder mirroring MULTIUSER_DEFAULTS.displayName ('Browser' in multiuser-settings-store.ts). It has to match the value that is actually sent to peers, so translating it would advertise a name the session never uses.
Product name in the About/Welcome header and version line — the same brand exception as SettingsPanel.tsx. The prose around it IS translated (shell:welcome.*).
Repository URL rendered as its own link text. A translated URL would not resolve.
Copyright notice. The legal entity and year are not localisable, and the AGPL header requires them verbatim.

Structural dump of a connection type's parameter signature (`req{a:float, b:int}`), assembled from user-defined parameter names and types. It is a signature, not a sentence — translating the braces or the `req`/`res` markers would misrepresent the schema.
The response half of the same parameter signature — see the `req{` entry.
Product name in the panel header — the same brand exception as SettingsPanel.tsx and WelcomeModal.tsx. Every sentence around it is translated (connect:*).
Example CIP routing path for an EtherNet/IP gateway, shown as a field placeholder. The value is what the user types verbatim; the Micro800 reference is an Allen-Bradley product name (ADR-0001 §6).
Example Keba browse-root names, shown as a placeholder. They are namespace identifiers on the controller, not words.
Example Denso controller name, shown as a placeholder. It is an identifier configured on the robot controller.
Example WinCaps project path, shown as a placeholder. A Windows path is not localisable.
Default SIMIT shared-memory name, shown as a placeholder. It must match the name RobotStudio's SIMIT connection opens, byte for byte.
